recipes.name: Saddle-Stitch Booklet
recipes.desc: Standard saddle-stitched booklet — the most common short-run binding.
recipes.input: Single PDF, sequential pages, count a multiple of 4, 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Keep page count ≤ 64 for saddle-stitch; enable creep on stock heavier than 100gsm.

recipes.name: Saddle-Stitch with Bleeds
recipes.desc: Saddle-stitch with synthetic bleed generation for artwork delivered without bleeds.
recipes.input: PDF at trim size (no bleed). Page count a multiple of 4.
recipes.tip: Synthetic bleeds are a rescue technique, not a replacement for real bleeds — flag it on the job ticket.

recipes.name: A5 Saddle-Stitch 2-Up on SRA3
recipes.desc: Impose A5 on SRA4 flats, then repeat two copies on SRA3.
recipes.input: A5 portrait PDF, sequential reading order, preferably 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Use Grid step-and-repeat (adapts to any booklet page count); SRA4 is exactly half of SRA3.

recipes.name: Perfect-Bound Book
recipes.desc: PUR/hot-melt perfect binding for books with 48+ pages.
recipes.input: Single PDF, sequential, 3mm bleed, CMYK. Count divisible by 8/16/32.
recipes.tip: Leave 5mm extra at the spine edge for PUR milling; confirm signature count with your bindery.

recipes.name: Perfect-Bound with Color Bar
recipes.desc: Perfect-bound signatures with inline color bars for press density control.
recipes.input: CMYK PDF, 3mm bleed, page count divisible by 16.
recipes.tip: Color bars need ≥ 8mm of non-image area along the gripper edge — verify plate size.

recipes.name: Case-Bound (Hardcover) Book
recipes.desc: Smyth-sewn case-bound book with signature imposition and spine marks.
recipes.input: Text-block PDF, sequential, 3mm bleed, CMYK. Cover supplied separately.
recipes.tip: Case-bound needs a separate cover imposition; add 3mm to the spine-side bleed for Smyth-sewing.

recipes.name: Zine / Mini Booklet
recipes.desc: Small-format DIY zine from a single sheet (8-page or 16-page fold).
recipes.input: 8-page or 16-page PDF at final reading size.
recipes.tip: For a single-sheet 8-page zine, print duplex, cut a centre slit and fold — verify with a paper dummy.

recipes.name: Comic Book Signatures
recipes.desc: Comic/graphic novel imposed in saddle-stitch or perfect-bound signatures.
recipes.input: Sequential pages at comic trim size + 3mm bleed. RGB or CMYK.
recipes.tip: US comic trim is 6.625×10.25"; manga is typically B6 (128×182mm). Confirm with the publisher spec.

recipes.name: Children's Book
recipes.desc: Full-color picture book with heavy stock and case binding.
recipes.input: Full-color CMYK PDF, min 300 DPI, 5mm bleed for board books.
recipes.tip: Board books need special imposition — each 'page' is two laminated sheets; confirm with the bindery.

recipes.name: Photo Book
recipes.desc: Lay-flat photo book with flush-mount or perfect binding.
recipes.input: High-res CMYK or sRGB PDF with 3mm bleed. Even page count.
recipes.tip: Lay-flat requires page pairs printed as spreads — a gutter gap will ruin panoramic photos.

recipes.name: Magazine Production
recipes.desc: Full commercial magazine with saddle-stitch or perfect binding and press marks.
recipes.input: Complete magazine PDF, sequential, CMYK, 3mm bleed, fonts embedded.
recipes.tip: Ads from multiple sources have inconsistent color — verify TIC does not exceed 340% for heatset web.

recipes.name: Catalog Signatures
recipes.desc: Multi-signature catalog for perfect binding on commercial presses.
recipes.input: CMYK PDF, page count divisible by signature size, 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Large catalogs (200+ pages) benefit from 32-up if your press handles the sheet — fewer signatures = fewer errors.

recipes.name: Annual Report
recipes.desc: Corporate annual report with mixed content and premium finishing.
recipes.input: CMYK + spot color PDF, 3mm bleed, fonts embedded, transparency flattened.
recipes.tip: If it mixes coated and uncoated stocks, impose each stock type separately and coordinate signature order.

recipes.name: Business Cards
recipes.desc: Standard multi-up business card layout on a press sheet.
recipes.input: Business card PDF at trim size with 3mm bleed. Duplex as pages 1 & 2.
recipes.tip: Standard sizes: 3.5×2" (US), 85×55mm (EU), 91×55mm (AU/NZ). Pull bleeds from the document.

recipes.name: Business Cards (No-Bleed Rescue)
recipes.desc: Business cards from artwork delivered without bleeds.
recipes.input: Business card PDF at exact trim size, no bleed.
recipes.tip: Synthetic bleeds on edge-to-edge photos show mirrored artefacts — request proper bleeds when possible.

recipes.name: Postcards
recipes.desc: Multi-up postcards (4×6 or A6) on press sheets.
recipes.input: Postcard PDF at trim size, front and back pages, 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: USPS requires min 3.5×5" and specific barcode clear zones for mailable postcards.

recipes.name: Greeting Cards
recipes.desc: Folded greeting cards imposed for duplex printing and fold finishing.
recipes.input: 4-page PDF in reading order at final folded size with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Greeting cards are typically 4 pages (front, inside-L, inside-R, back) — the booklet tool reorders spreads.

recipes.name: Playing Cards
recipes.desc: Full deck of playing cards imposed for sheet-fed printing.
recipes.input: 54 cards as individual pages, poker size (63×88mm) with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Playing cards need exact front-to-back registration or the back pattern reveals the face at the edges.

recipes.name: Door Hangers
recipes.desc: Multi-up door hangers with a die-cut hook hole.
recipes.input: Door hanger PDF at trim size with die-cut hook area marked. 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Standard door hanger is 4.25×11". Use the cut-contour tool to define the hook die precisely.

recipes.name: Rack Cards
recipes.desc: 4×9 inch rack cards imposed for multi-up printing.
recipes.input: Rack card PDF at 4×9" trim size with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Rack cards have a narrow aspect — run the grain parallel to the long edge for stiffness.

recipes.name: Numbered Tickets
recipes.desc: Sequential numbered tickets with cut-and-stack imposition.
recipes.input: PDF with one page per ticket, sequentially numbered. Count divisible by grid cells.
recipes.tip: Cut-and-stack numbering needs the shuffle order to match your guillotine cut sequence — verify with a test sheet.

recipes.name: Variable Data Tickets
recipes.desc: Tickets with variable data (barcodes, names, seats) imposed efficiently.
recipes.input: PDF with one ticket per page, each containing unique variable data.
recipes.tip: Variable data tickets need each barcode unique and scannable — verify readability at final printed size.

recipes.name: Wedding Invitations
recipes.desc: Premium invitations with RSVP cards and envelopes imposed together.
recipes.input: Separate PDFs for each suite component (invite, RSVP, details), each at trim size with bleed.
recipes.tip: Wedding suites often include multiple card sizes — gang them so all pieces print in the same pass with identical color.

recipes.name: Sticker Sheets
recipes.desc: Full sticker sheets with kiss-cut contours for peel-and-stick.
recipes.input: Individual sticker artwork as separate pages. 1mm bleed around each.
recipes.tip: Kiss-cut depth penetrates the vinyl/paper but NOT the liner; keep ≥ 3mm padding for plotter tracking.

recipes.name: Die-Cut Stickers
recipes.desc: Individual die-cut stickers (through-cut, no backing sheet).
recipes.input: Individual sticker designs, one per page, at final size with 1mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Thru-cut on vinyl needs a slightly oversized cut path (0.5mm offset) to avoid white borders from misregistration.

recipes.name: Product Labels
recipes.desc: Multi-up product labels for bottles, jars and boxes.
recipes.input: Label PDF at flat die size with 2mm bleed. CMYK + spot if brand-critical.
recipes.tip: Labels for curved surfaces (bottles) need distortion compensation — confirm values with the applicator vendor.

recipes.name: Shipping Labels
recipes.desc: Shipping labels (4×6") on self-adhesive A4/Letter sheets.
recipes.input: 4×6" label PDF per shipment, one page per label.
recipes.tip: Shipping labels are usually thermal-printed; for offset/digital use a label-stock template and align to the die exactly.

recipes.name: Address Labels
recipes.desc: Avery-style address labels on standard label sheets.
recipes.input: Individual label content, one per page, at the Avery cell size.
recipes.tip: Pre-die-cut label stock needs exact registration — test-print on plain paper and hold against a sheet first.

recipes.name: Vinyl Stickers
recipes.desc: Outdoor-rated vinyl stickers with laminate overprint and contour cut.
recipes.input: Sticker artwork on transparent background (PNG/PDF) at final size.
recipes.tip: For outdoor vinyl add a 2mm white border to prevent edge peel; use solvent or UV-cure inks only.

recipes.name: QR Code Labels
recipes.desc: Unique QR code labels for product tracking or authentication.
recipes.input: One QR code per page, or a data file for batch generation. Label size specified.
recipes.tip: QR codes need min 15mm at print resolution; add error-correction level H (30%) for labels that may get scratched.

recipes.name: Coasters
recipes.desc: Printed coasters (round or square) imposed for die cutting.
recipes.input: Coaster artwork at die size (typically 95mm round/square) with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Coaster board (1.4mm pulpboard) absorbs ink differently — reduce TIC to 280% and expect color shift.

recipes.name: Box Layout
recipes.desc: Folding carton box flat (die-line) with artwork positioned for die cutting.
recipes.input: Flat artwork matching the die-line exactly. Die-line supplied as a separate overlay PDF.
recipes.tip: Always work from the die-maker's approved CAD file — even 0.5mm off can jam the gluing machine.

recipes.name: Label Wrap
recipes.desc: Wraparound labels for bottles/cans/tubes with distortion compensation.
recipes.input: Flat label artwork at unwrapped dimensions with 2mm bleed. Specify diameter.
recipes.tip: distortion% = (thickness / (diameter/2 + thickness)) × 100. Round containers need only circumferential distortion.

recipes.name: Corrugated Packaging
recipes.desc: Large-format corrugated box or display printed on flatbed or flexo.
recipes.input: Artwork on the corrugated die flat. Spot colors preferred. Verify flute direction.
recipes.tip: Corrugated print is low resolution (65-100 LPI) — simplify halftones, min type 8pt, avoid reverses < 10pt.

recipes.name: Bag Layout
recipes.desc: Paper or poly bag printed flat and imposed for production.
recipes.input: Flat bag artwork with fold lines marked. Gusset panels if applicable.
recipes.tip: Bag printing wraps around fold edges; side gusset panels are often printed in mirror — verify with a folding dummy.

recipes.name: Sleeve / Band
recipes.desc: Shrink sleeves or belly bands for product packaging.
recipes.input: Flat sleeve artwork at pre-shrink dimensions. Specify shrink material and container.
recipes.tip: Shrink sleeves distort differently circumferentially vs vertically — get the exact shrink ratios from your converter.

recipes.name: Envelope Layout
recipes.desc: Printed envelopes imposed for flatbed or rotary die cutting.
recipes.input: Envelope artwork on the flat die layout with fold flaps. Die template as overlay.
recipes.tip: Envelope flaps must be oriented for the fold direction — print on the inside of the flap if the design wraps the seal.

recipes.name: Poster Tiling
recipes.desc: Large poster split into printable tiles with overlap for assembly.
recipes.input: Single-page PDF at full poster size (e.g. 24×36" or A0). 150-300 DPI.
recipes.tip: Use 10-15mm overlap between tiles; align the tile grid to avoid splitting faces/text across a seam.

recipes.name: Banner Printing
recipes.desc: Wide-format banners with tiling for roll-fed printers.
recipes.input: Single PDF at final banner size or at 1/4 scale. Specify dimensions.
recipes.tip: Banners viewed at 3+ metres need only 72-100 DPI; vinyl banners need a 25mm hemming allowance.

recipes.name: Signage Repeat
recipes.desc: Repeated signage (shelf talkers, aisle signs) ganged on large-format sheets.
recipes.input: Single sign PDF at trim size with 3mm bleed. Specify substrate sheet dimensions.
recipes.tip: For rigid substrates add 3mm bleed beyond the cut; the CNC router kerf is 2-3mm — account for it in gutters.

recipes.name: Trade Show Panels
recipes.desc: Multi-panel trade show displays split for separate printing and assembly.
recipes.input: Full continuous artwork at the assembled display size. Specify frame system + panel count.
recipes.tip: Trade-show frame systems have pockets that add 25-50mm per side — get exact frame specs before sizing panels.

recipes.name: Floor Graphics
recipes.desc: Floor decals and wayfinding graphics with contour cutting.
recipes.input: Floor graphic artwork at final size. Include 10mm bleed for contour shapes.
recipes.tip: Floor graphics must be laminated with anti-slip overlaminate (ASTM D2047) — always specify the laminate.

recipes.name: Vehicle Wrap
recipes.desc: Vehicle wrap panels split for contour-cut application.
recipes.input: Full vehicle artwork on a professional template. Panels pre-separated or as one flat.
recipes.tip: Vehicle wraps need 50-75mm extra per panel for wrapping edges — use a professional template, not hand-measured.

recipes.name: Full Press Marks
recipes.desc: Complete press mark set for commercial offset production.
recipes.input: Already-imposed press sheet PDF ready for mark application.
recipes.tip: Standard mark set for any commercial offset job — place marks ≥ 3mm from trim and keep them from overlapping.

recipes.name: Digital Press Ready
recipes.desc: Mark set optimized for digital presses (HP Indigo, Xerox iGen).
recipes.input: Imposed PDF, any tool. CMYK with transparency flattened.
recipes.tip: Digital presses have built-in registration — focus on color bars and trim marks to keep the DFE file simple.

recipes.name: Offset Press Ready
recipes.desc: Full offset press preparation with all required finishing marks.
recipes.input: Imposed press-sheet PDF, CMYK, transparency flattened, fonts embedded.
recipes.tip: Verify the plate accommodates all marks — on CTP workflows marks are often added by the CTP software.

recipes.name: Saddle-Stitch Finishing Marks
recipes.desc: Finishing marks specifically for saddle-stitch bindery operations.
recipes.input: Imposed saddle-stitch signatures, ready for finishing marks.
recipes.tip: The saddle-stitch line reads collating marks optically — ensure high contrast and consistent placement.

recipes.name: Perfect Bind Finishing Marks
recipes.desc: Finishing marks for perfect binding with gathering verification.
recipes.input: Imposed perfect-bind signatures with known signature thickness.
recipes.tip: OMR and gathering marks serve different purposes — gathering is visual, OMR is machine-verified. Use both on high-volume runs.

recipes.name: Die-Cut Production Marks
recipes.desc: Complete die-cutting mark set for labels, stickers and packaging.
recipes.input: Artwork with die-line paths on separate spot-color layers, imposed on the press sheet.
recipes.tip: Use industry layer naming: CutContour, KissCut, Crease, Perforation — automated cutters recognise these from the metadata.

recipes.name: Watermarked Proof
recipes.desc: Draft proof with watermark and job info for client approval.
recipes.input: Any PDF at any stage. This is a proofing overlay, not production output.
recipes.tip: Always watermark proofs before sending to clients — an unwatermarked proof has reached press in every shop.

recipes.name: Branded Proof
recipes.desc: Client proof with your shop's branding, job info and color patches.
recipes.input: PDF to be proofed, at any stage of production.
recipes.tip: Include your shop's ICC profile name in the footer so the client can identify the proofing condition.

recipes.name: Wall Calendar
recipes.desc: 12-month wall calendar with saddle-stitch or wire-o binding.
recipes.input: 13-page PDF (cover + 12 months) in landscape with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Wall calendars need a hanging hole — add a drill mark top-center; wire-o is preferred so pages lay flat.

recipes.name: Desk Calendar
recipes.desc: Desk tent calendar with fold-and-stand construction.
recipes.input: 13-page PDF at the flat (unfolded) desk size with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Desk calendars fold in half to stand — the base half is usually blank; ensure front/back align for the fold.

recipes.name: Planner / Diary
recipes.desc: Wire-o or perfect-bound planner with weekly/daily layouts.
recipes.input: Complete planner PDF, sequential, 3mm bleed. Count divisible by signature size.
recipes.tip: Wire-o planners need a 12mm margin on the bind side for wire holes; perfect-bound need 5mm spine milling.

recipes.name: Restaurant Menu
recipes.desc: Folded restaurant menu (bi-fold, tri-fold, or booklet).
recipes.input: Menu PDF in reading-order pages, final folded size with 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: Menus on heavy stock (300gsm+) must be scored before folding or the paper cracks — add scoring marks.

recipes.name: Newsletter
recipes.desc: Folded newsletter (4-8 pages) for mailing or distribution.
recipes.input: 4-page or 8-page newsletter PDF in reading order, folded size, 3mm bleed.
recipes.tip: For self-mailers the address panel must meet USPS regulations: clear zone around the barcode, correct fold-edge placement.

recipes.name: Envelope Production
recipes.desc: Printed envelopes imposed and prepared for envelope-making machinery.
recipes.input: Flat envelope artwork on the die-maker template with fold flaps.
recipes.tip: Window envelopes need the window precisely registered to the letter fold — test with the actual insert.

recipes.name: Mixed Gang Run
recipes.desc: Multiple different jobs ganged on a single press sheet for cost efficiency.
recipes.input: Multiple job PDFs at their individual trim sizes with bleed. Same stock and coating.
recipes.tip: Gang runs share ink density — group items with similar color requirements (e.g. all warm tones together).

recipes.name: Gang Run with Full Marks
recipes.desc: Ganged production sheet with complete finishing marks for commercial press.
recipes.input: Multiple production-ready PDFs, trimmed to final size with 3mm bleed. Same substrate.
recipes.tip: Number each ganged item in the slug so the cutter operator can verify all pieces after cutting.

recipes.name: Expert Custom Imposition
recipes.desc: Fully custom imposition using Expert Grid for non-standard layouts.
recipes.input: Source pages ready for custom positioning. Know your press sheet size and grid requirements.
recipes.tip: Expert Grid is the escape hatch for layouts no standard tool handles — plan your grid on paper first.

recipes.name: Expert Grid with Finishing
recipes.desc: Custom Expert Grid imposition with full finishing marks.
recipes.input: Source pages and a detailed imposition plan (grid spec, gutter widths, rotations).
recipes.tip: Verify finishing marks do not overlap the grid cells — custom gutters may be narrower than the mark footprint.

recipes.name: Cut-and-Stack Numbering
recipes.desc: Sequential numbering with cut-and-stack page ordering for tickets, NCR or raffle books.
recipes.input: PDF with one page per numbered item, sequentially numbered. Count = grid cells × sheet count.
recipes.tip: The shuffle order MUST match your cutting sequence (top-to-bottom then left-to-right). Verify a test sheet first.

recipes.name: Print-Ready Preparation
recipes.desc: Standard pre-flight and preparation workflow for incoming files.
recipes.input: Any incoming PDF from a client or designer. No specific format required.
recipes.tip: First-pass workflow for every incoming file — run preflight first, then convert and optimize. Never skip preflight.

recipes.name: Preflight and Fix
recipes.desc: Identify and repair common PDF issues before production.
recipes.input: Problematic PDF that crashes, shows errors, or renders incorrectly.
recipes.tip: If repair fails the file may be too damaged — re-save as PDF/X in Acrobat, or distill from PostScript as a last resort.

recipes.name: Multi-File Merge
recipes.desc: Merge multiple source files into a single document for unified processing.
recipes.input: Multiple PDFs to be combined. Specify the desired page order.
recipes.tip: Merge order becomes page order — double-check the sequence; convert to a common color profile before merging.

recipes.name: Duplex Interleave
recipes.desc: Interleave separate front and back files for duplex printing.
recipes.input: Two PDFs: one with all fronts, one with all backs. Both must have the same page count.
recipes.tip: If the back file is in reverse order (common from scanning), reverse it first — one page off cascades through the whole job.

recipes.name: Work and Tumble
recipes.desc: Flip backup for the work-and-tumble duplex printing method.
recipes.input: Imposed front-side sheet ready for tumble backup creation.
recipes.tip: Work-and-tumble flips along the short edge; work-and-turn along the long edge — the wrong flip mirrors the backs.

recipes.name: Landscape Rotation
recipes.desc: Rotate pages from portrait to landscape (or vice versa) for press feed direction.
recipes.input: PDF with pages in the wrong orientation for the target press.
recipes.tip: Confirm rotation direction (CW vs CCW) with a test page — the wrong rotation puts the gripper edge on the wrong side.

recipes.name: Flexo Distortion
recipes.desc: Pre-distort artwork for flexographic plate mounting on cylinders.
recipes.input: Artwork at 1:1 undistorted size. Specify plate thickness and cylinder repeat length.
recipes.tip: D% = (plate thickness × π / repeat length) × 100. Always get these values from the plate maker.
